tests.title: The flags exist, --adversarial is off by default and the round limit is 1 when only --adversarial is given
given: the spec command's flag set
tests.when: the flags are parsed with no arguments, with `--adversarial`, and with `--adversarial --adversarial-rounds 3`
then: adversarial is false when not given
adversarial is true and the resulting Options round limit is 1 with `--adversarial` alone
the round limit is 3 when `--adversarial-rounds 3` is given
tests.pseudocode: o = specOptions(parse([])); assert !o.Adversarial; o = specOptions(parse(['--adversarial'])); assert o.Adversarial && o.AdversarialRounds == 1; o = specOptions(parse(['--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds','3'])); assert o.AdversarialRounds == 3

tests.title: A round count outside 1 to 5, including an explicit 0, is a usage error with or without --preflight
given: a stub provider and a fetch hook that fail the test if called
an empty specs dir
tests.when: spec runs with `--adversarial --adversarial-rounds N` for N in 0, 6 and -1, each with and without `--preflight`
then: the exit code is 2
the envelope error category is `usage`
no model call and no input fetch happened
usage.phases is empty and no file was written
tests.pseudocode: for n in [0,6,-1]: for pf in [false,true]: r = runSpec(args(n, pf)); assert r.exit == 2; assert r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert fetchCalls == 0 && modelCalls == 0; assert len(r.env.usage.phases) == 0; assert dirEmpty(specsDir)

tests.title: --adversarial-rounds without --adversarial is a usage error before anything is fetched
given: a stub provider and a fetch hook that fail the test if called
tests.when: spec runs with `--adversarial-rounds 2`, with and without `--preflight`
then: the exit code is 2
the error category is `usage`
no model was called, nothing was fetched, no phase recorded and no file written
tests.pseudocode: for pf in [false,true]: r = runSpec(['--adversarial-rounds','2'] + pf); assert r.exit == 2 && r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert modelCalls == 0 && fetchCalls == 0

tests.title: A non-integer --adversarial-rounds value is rejected by the flag parser as a usage error
given: a stub provider that fails the test if called
tests.when: spec runs with `--adversarial --adversarial-rounds abc` and with `--adversarial-rounds 1.5`
then: the exit code is 2
the error category is `usage`
no model was called and nothing was fetched
tests.pseudocode: for v in ['abc','1.5']: r = runSpec(['--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds',v]); assert r.exit == 2; assert r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert modelCalls == 0

tests.title: Without --adversarial the run has the same phases, result, summary, files and usage as before the feature
given: the real specgen pipeline over the valid_spec fixture with a scripted author and a reviewer fake that fails the test if called
Adversarial is off
tests.when: an undivided input is run to completion
then: the phases run are exactly prd, requirements, test_spec and tasks
no package carries a `review` field in the JSON result
the summary sentence has no `review:` clause
the package directory holds only the files the format defines
usage.phases[] names are exactly prd, requirements, test_spec, tasks
tests.pseudocode: res = Run(ctx, opts{Adversarial:false}); assert phaseNames(res) == ['prd','requirements','test_spec','tasks']; assert reviewerCalls == 0; assert !contains(json(res), '"review"'); assert !contains(res.Summary(), 'review:')

tests.title: A dry run with --adversarial runs the review phases, writes nothing and reports the same review as a real run
given: the real pipeline with scripted author, reviewer and reviser returning a major finding then no findings
two runs of the same input: one with --dry-run, one real
tests.when: both runs complete
then: the dry run invoked prd_review and prd_revision
the dry run wrote no file
the dry run's package review equals the real run's package review field by field
tests.pseudocode: d = Run(opts{DryRun:true, Adversarial:true, Rounds:2}); r = Run(opts{Adversarial:true, Rounds:2}); assert noFiles(dryDir); assert d.Package.Review == r.Package.Review

tests.title: The review phase is a fresh conversation sent the PRD, input, context, labelled notes, run context and read-only tools
given: a recording runner that captures the agentrun.Phase of every call
a PRD with open questions, relevant files and codebase_notes 'NOTE-X', input text and `--context` text
tests.when: the review phase of round 1 runs
then: the phase Kind is prd_review and its name is `prd_review`
the prompt contains the spec name, title, body, an open question and a relevant file of the PRD
the prompt contains the original input and the --context text
the notes appear labelled as the author's claims to be checked against the code, not as facts
the system prompt carries the language block, steering, repository map and landscape of existing specs
the built-in tools are the read-only file tools, plus code_search when the index exists
the prompt is not a continuation of the PRD phase's conversation
tests.pseudocode: ph = recorder.last(); assert ph.Kind == 'prd_review'; assert contains(ph.User, prd.Body) && contains(ph.User, 'NOTE-X'); assert contains(ph.User, 'claims') && contains(ph.User, 'not facts'); assert ph.BuiltinTools == WithCodeSearch(ReadOnlyFileTools, cs); assert ph.History == nil

tests.title: A review of a split scope is told the split but not given the PRD-writing instructions

the prompt states that work belonging to another scope is not a dropped ask
the prompt does not contain the PRD-writing instructions of the split block

tests.title: The review system prompt names every flaw kind and tells the reviewer not to approve

tests.pseudocode: s = prdReviewSystemPrompt(); for k in flawKindKeywords: assert contains(lower(s), k); assert contains(lower(s), 'not approve') or contains(lower(s), 'do not approve')

tests.title: The review tool accepts an empty list and a valid finding with severity enum and all fields

tests.title: Evidence comparison ignores only whitespace differences
given: the evidence normalisation function used for the repeat check
tests.when: for any two strings a and b, where b is a with leading and trailing whitespace added and internal whitespace runs replaced by runs of other whitespace characters, and for any pair that differs in a non-whitespace character
then: normalised equality holds for the whitespace-only variants
normalised equality does not hold when a non-whitespace character differs
tests.pseudocode: for a in gen_strings(): b = perturbWhitespace(a); assert sameEvidence(a,b); c = mutateNonSpaceChar(a); assert !sameEvidence(a,c)

tests.title: For any round limit and outcome sequence the loop runs at most the limit of reviews and ends with exactly one stop reason, incomplete winning
given: a round loop driven by scripted reviewer and reviser outcomes (findings of any severity mix, empty, failure, budget stop)

tests.title: A failed review or revision stops the rounds, warns high and leaves the exit code alone
